The app is built at `/private/tmp/dsb-eval/opus-5-5/A-prime-5`. It compiles with no errors, and the main flows pass in a headless browser.

**What I checked in the browser (Playwright, 1280px wide):**
- Submitting the login form empty puts both fields into an error state with a message. Logging in with `admin` / `admin` goes to `/dashboard`.
- The dashboard shows all 8 tiles, and the log adds a new line every 3 seconds.
- The profile menu stays fully on screen: its right edge is at x=1248 in a 1280px window. Clicking outside closes it.
- Users: the 5 seeded members load. Edit (PUT), Invite (POST) and Delete (DELETE) each changed the table as expected. "Delete user" in the edit dialog opens the delete confirmation with the same member still selected. Clicking the backdrop closes the delete dialog. Sign Out works.
- The browser console showed no errors.

**Bugs found and fixed while testing:**
- Save and Send Invite did nothing at first, because the dialog forms' submit events were never wired up.
- Log timestamps were in UTC instead of local time.

One test run failed when the delete dialog didn't close on a backdrop click. The same step passed when I ran it on its own, so I treated it as a timing problem in the test script. I made the bar chart shorter to match Figma's proportions after the last screenshot, and haven't looked at it since.

**Styling.** Every colour, font size, radius and shadow uses the `:root` values you gave, plus the `.tag` classes. Figma uses values outside that set (greys like `#888`/`#555`/`#EBEBEB`, sizes 13/15/20/22/26px, 12px radii), and I rounded each to the nearest given value. The one colour not taken directly from the list is the "Delete" button outline, which I made by mixing `--color-danger` with white. Text uses the system font stack from the styleguide, not Inter.

**Where Figma and the spec disagree, I followed the spec's content and Figma's layout and spacing:**
- **Login:** I left out the "Blueprint" heading and the divider that Figma shows, because the spec says to add nothing else. The text is the spec's wording.
- **Dashboard:** Figma's tiles have different numbers, labels and services, and a 6-bar hourly chart. I used the spec's values, the 7 days, the 5 services, and an uppercase title on each metric tile. I kept Figma's "System Overview" heading and "Last updated" line, since neither is a tile.
- **Dashboard layout:** Figma has no standalone Data Summary tile and shows logs as an event list. I laid it out as four metric tiles on top, then Throughput and Service Health, then Data Summary and a dark monospace log panel.
- **Header:** Figma's nav links (Overview/Metrics/Logs/Settings) can't reach `/users`, so I used Dashboard/Users. I dropped the "Online" tag next to the avatar.
- **Footer:** the spec asks for brand, link columns and a legal row; Figma only shows copyright and two links. I built the spec's version, and the column link names are made up.
- **Users table:** separate Avatar and Name columns as the spec says, not Figma's combined USER column. The action buttons follow the spec's emphasis (Details plainest, Delete red), where Figma has Edit as the plain one.
- **Badge colours:** Admin is red, Editor blue, Viewer grey; Active is green, Inactive grey. An upward error-rate trend is red ("negative"), where Figma shows amber.

**Not covered by Figma:** the delete dialog, invite dialog, profile menu, the logo mark and the footer columns. I designed these myself in the same style.

To run it: `npx @angular/cli@19 serve`. Port 4311 was already in use by another process on this machine, so I tested on 4597.
